best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Havoc DMG% boost and up to an additional 30% Havoc DMG% after you land 4 Basic or Heavy Attacks for a grand total of 40% additional Havoc damage after fully ramped.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Offers an unconditional 12% Havoc DMG and 12% Basic Attack DMG boost when placed in the Main Echo slot, making it a solid choice for Havoc focused resonators who emphasize Basic Attack damage and are looking to use the 5P Sunk-Sinking Eclipse set bonus.

best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional ATK% boost and an additional 5% ATK% for every 1.5 seconds the equipped character has been in combat - up to 20% after 6 seconds, totalling 30% additional ATK% after fully ramped. This set almost almost loses out to most characters signature elemental sets, but is generically usable across all damage characters regardless of their element.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Very easy echo to use that should be used at the very beginning of the burst window right after the Intro. Thanks to its instant cast there is no thinking required and you can enjoy your ATK% boost and some nice burst damage.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Camellya's Signature is strong on a lot of Sword users, but is in particular designed for her since a lot of extra Basic Attack DMG Bonus is only exploitable if Camellya's Concerto is spent mid-rotation, which is a mechanic only she has access to, making it the best for her by a lot.

cons: Very old DPS, has not gotten a rerun in ages to take advantage of her sequence value and is way behind the current damage ceiling of the game despite teammate and main Echo upgrades since release;

Very prone to interruption on her highest-damaging attack until S1, plus Inherent Skills do not fully make her immune to getting interrupted during her spinning attacks, inconsistent character against boss enemies overall;

Her White Hair rotation is too long to be ideal for maximizing DPS, meaning optimally she relies on bad tracking against bosses, which only further contributes to inconsistency issues. Speaking of which, even her faster Red Hair rotation is the longest DPS rotation in the game and Outro Buffs are prone to running out near the end, where a lot of Camellya's damage lies;

All her premium teammates can and will be used up by stronger characters, often relegating her to weaker fallback options like Sanhua and Danjin that may make her struggle to clear modern endgame content.
pros: Super F2P-friendly AoE DPS can use completely free teammates and weapons and yield great results;
Can switch between a more AoE and single-target-oriented playstyle to suit her needs;
Great sequence value compared to most 1.x characters;

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Camellya is a 5-star Havoc Sword main damage dealer known for having one of, if not the longest, rotation times of any Main DPS character in the game. She deals the greatest portion of Echo damage among any non-Echo damage dealer thanks to her dedicated Echo Nightmare: Crownless that she can incorporate into her extensive rotations for a strong mix of Basic, Liberation and Echo damage. While her most optimized rotations don't feature many Swap cancels, she makes up for it in her ability to optimize via several Echo Animation cancels in her long Hypercarry rotations and playstyle.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics
paragraphs: Camellya's main rotation goals are to consume her Forte gauges by filling up her Concerto gauge 2 times: 1 to cast an enhanced Skill that deals massive damage, 1 for her actual Outro.

Her Forte gauge is called Crimson Pistils, and she can hold up to 100 of them at once. They are only restored via her Intro and her Forte Skill, called Ephemeral. Therefore, rotating with Camellya before an Intro is available is not useful, since she cannot make progress towards the latter half of her rotation, where most of her damage lies.

Camellya may consume Crimson Pistils via Skills and Basic/Heavy/Mid-air Attacks. Her Skill switches her form, of which she has 2, marked by her hair colour, which can either be white (standard form) or red (Blossom Mode). For simplicity's sake, they are commonly referred to as White Hair and Red Hair mode.

In White Hair mode, Camellya is on the ground and free to move as she desires. Her attacks are additionally longer and more single-target oriented. However, in Red Hair mode, she becomes unable to move, aside from dodges (and jumps/unenhanced skills that switch her back to White Hair mode as well). But in exchange, her attacks become faster and more capable in AoE. As Basic Attacks consume Crimson Pistils, Camellya accumulates up to 10 Crimson Buds, each empowering the state that follows the cast of her Forte Skill.

Her Forte Skill consumes 70 Concerto Energy when built to full, and Camellya enters Budding Mode. In this mode, the DMG multiplier of all her attacks except her Ultimate are increased by 50% (+5% per Crimson Bud consumed). This mode ends if Camellya is switched out, or if she runs out of Crimson Pistils again.

sections.heading: Rotation, Benefits & Shortcomings
paragraphs: Camellya's rotation is very extensive, as it requires her to fill up her Concerto Gauge essentially twice. For that, she has no faster way to do so than by holding down the Basic Attack button after immediately entering her faster Red Hair mode through her Skill. This makes Camellya spin in place in a wide AoE, and it is her fastest way of consuming Crimson Pistils. Though, she will need to fully cast this spin animation twice, plus 2 Skills (one to enter and one to exit Red Hair mode), plus her Intro and Ultimate. Her Echo casts can additionally be weaved in and immediately Dash Cancelled after some animations that are beneficial to Dash Cancel anyways, but in spite of these optimizations, Camellya's rotation exceeds the 15-second mark, which means by the end of it, 14s Outro buffs have already expired.

This means that if Camellya gets interrupted at any point, which can happen, including during her Forte Skill which fully cancels its massive damage, this rotation can and will get even longer, which means half or more of the highest-damaging portion of her rotation, Budding Mode, can lose out on game-changing Outro buffs, and there is nothing Camellya can do about it other than try fighting more passive enemies.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: Overall, Camellya's very long, backloaded rotation means that she has a hard time keeping her damage consistent, and that she may also execute fewer rotations within allocated endgame timespans than most characters in the game, overall making her final performances subpar, especially if her rotation isn't fully optimized to weave in extra Echo casts.

Despite Camellya's massive advantages of having easy access to F2P-friendly teammates like Sanhua and Danjin, as well as a good F2P weapon option in the form of Emerald of Genesis, she has trouble delivering on a proper standard of performance in spite of her theoretically strong damage per rotation, because in practice those rotations take too long to execute and are inconsistent. Not to mention, nowadays, Camellya's best team has barely gotten an upgrade with Lynae and Mornye's release, and she's otherwise still stuck to the Sanhua/Roccia+Shorekeeper that frankly don't deliver buffs-wise as much as Camellya could hope. Plus, Camellya's own damage per rotation standard barely delivers compared to the powerhouses of today.

In conclusion, while Camellya has massive upsides in terms of F2P-friendliness and ease of use, they don't come without severe downsides. Rotation inconsistency and excessive length, plus the lack of performance and new teammates to back up her meta stance, do not make her a valuable character to own in the current state of the game, making her difficult meta position rather forgettable, but still capable of delivering (although at a low standard) with very budgeted investments under the right conditions.

synergies.commentary: The best Hybrid choices for Camellya, Lynae generally being the best as her generalist buffs are too many to count and make Camellya's damage skyrocket. Roccia is another one of her premium options, very comparable to Sanhua as they each provide great ATK and Basic Attack DMG Amplification buffs for her, Sanhua generally being the best F2P choice and better than Roccia if she doesn't have her Signature; Danjin is an additional option if Sanhua is already taken elsewhere as she also gives a solid general Havoc DMG Amplification buff on her Outro.

These 3 are the best generalist Supports in the game. Mornye has a special synergy with Lynae since Lynae can apply Tune Rupture/Strain for Mornye to respond to them and provide her full array of buffs, making her the best choice if Lynae is in use. Shorekeeper is however a close second thanks to her massive CRIT buffs and other generalist buffs, then Verina is the most accessible and still very strong option if neither are available.
